site: any employer on Phenom People's careers widget / Oracle Recruiting Cloud, confirmed on ADT Careers (jobs.adt.com)
class: A page classifier and its two downstream handlers whose every rule for 'this is an account/registration step' assumes a password field exists, so a genuinely passwordless registration gate is read as not-an-account-page and falls to generic form filling
symptom: ADT Careers' application stopped with 'the application form bounced back to the job posting' after the circuit breaker caught repeated identical attempts, with no mention of the actual blocker -- a required, unticked 'I agree with the terms and conditions' checkbox on a registration gate that never asks for a password at all.
root_cause: The page was Phenom People's 'Authentication screen. You don't need to have an account': an email box, a honeypot, and a required terms checkbox, then Next -- no password field anywhere. account_state.read_state() classifies every account/registration state from the number of password boxes; zero passwords and no sign-in wording fell through every rule to NONE, so the page was never routed to handle_auth_gate at all. Even with classification fixed, handle_auth_gate's own pw_count==0 branch returned False immediately (never tried fill_create_account_form), and fill_create_account_form's own entry guard required at least one password box before it would even look at the form's checkboxes -- so the already-correct, already-broad acknowledgement logic (acknowledgements.is_acknowledgement, f336) that would tick a routine terms-and-conditions box never got a chance to run. Generic page_agent filling left the checkbox unticked (correctly) but had no reason to withhold the page's Next button, clicked it anyway, and the site's own validation bounced the page back until the circuit breaker stopped the run with its generic message.
why_tests_missed: Every existing account_state.py and fill_create_account_form test fixture has at least one password field (a Create Account form, a Sign In form, or an EMAIL_FIRST sign-in-first page); none modeled a registration gate that never asks for a password at all, so the zero-password path through the classifier and both handlers was never exercised.
fix: account_state.read_state() gained a pattern for this wording ('you don't need an account', 'get started ... using your email') that classifies a zero-password page with an email box as CREATE_FORM instead of NONE. browser_automation.handle_auth_gate's pw_count==0 branch now routes to fill_create_account_form (guarded by account_on_record()) instead of returning False immediately, mirroring its existing pw_count>=2 sibling branch. fill_create_account_form's entry guard, password-pair-confirmation check, and its Next/Continue button fallback are now conditional on pw_fields being non-empty instead of assuming at least one password box; the checkbox-ticking logic itself (acknowledgements.is_acknowledgement, safety.is_attestation) needed no change -- it already ticks this exact class of box once the page reaches it. Not changed: SubmissionGuardV0's click-authorization heuristic still requires a classic two-password form with a literal Create Account/Register/Sign Up button before it will approve the final click, so a passwordless gate's own 'Next' button still stops the run for the owner's one click -- deliberately out of scope here (BEHAVIOUR.md documents the boundary).
prevention: A new project's account/registration-step classifier and form filler should treat 'how many password fields' as one signal among several, never a gate that a genuinely passwordless flow cannot pass at all -- test at least one zero-password registration fixture from the start, alongside the create/sign-in/email-first ones, and keep the click-authorization heuristic and the consent-classification policy as two separate decisions so loosening one never silently loosens the other.
